free_tier.stated: Monthly Plan: 5 Static Visible IPv6 Tunnels (VIPs), 1 Gbps Encrypted Tunnels, Free IPv4 Reverse Proxy, Port Forwarding, Tier-1 Bandwidth, Unmetered Traffic, $6.95/mo.

record.interface_detail: Cloud Seeder installers for Windows and macOS, or manual setup with their addresses
record.tooling: Cloud Seeder (their client) or a manual WireGuard configuration
record.chaining: a paid alternative to Route64 for the same job: a routed public prefix onto a machine that has no public address
record.binding_note: Unmetered traffic and 1 Gbps tunnels, so nothing in the vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month. The gate is the subscription price, which is not a limit kind.

identity_cost.detail: paid plan at $6.95/month; sign-in is by email address and the plan is bought, so a payment method is implied by the price and was not read as a form.

record.reliability_note: single small operator; the free IPv4 reverse proxy is listed as a feature of a paid plan, so a client without IPv6 cannot reach a service here without that proxy.
record.confidence_note: the page is a client-rendered application; the price block was read from the rendered crawl, not the raw HTML, which returned a template shell.

evidence.proved: 'Unmetered Traffic', '5 Static Visible IPv6 Tunnels (VIPs)', 'Port Forwarding' and '$6.95/mo'
a user that installs the tunnel, distributed as a signed installer

record.notes: No free tier and no trial stated. The raw HTML is a Shells white-label shell titled 'KLB Vue Template' with a Realm name of shells.com, so nothing is readable without rendering; the numbers above come from the rendered markdown. Port forwarding on a public IPv6 is the ingress, so UDP is carried as routed IP rather than as a vendor feature.

extras.wg_detail: No .conf is published without an account. Their client sets the tunnel up: 'Instantly launch and self host your favorite internet appliances with a click using Cloud Seeder ... or use our IPs to manually setup your own.' WireGuard is the sponsor logo and the transport in the how-it-works diagram.
extras.transit_note: IPv6rs carries the tunnel and its upstreams carry the routed prefix
